pr_title: templates: Delete file headers on any template error
pr_body:
Closes #8147

A template that fails to parse or execute left the `Content-Length`, `Content-Type`, `Etag`, `Last-Modified` and `Accept-Ranges` headers from `file_server` on the error response. The client got a 500 that declared the file's size and had no body (or, with `handle_errors`, a shorter body than declared).

#5905 already deleted these headers for `{{httpError}}`. This change deletes the same headers in `executeTemplate`'s error branch, so every template error gets the same clean response. `funcHTTPError` is left as is, because the browse template in `file_server` also calls it.

Test: `TestServeHTTPErrorDeletesFileHeaders` in `modules/caddyhttp/templates/templates_test.go` covers `{{httpError 404}}`, an unknown function and a failed `include`. The last two fail without the change and pass with it. `go test ./...` passes.

Manual check with the Caddyfile from the issue: before, `curl -v /bad.html` gives `500`, `Content-Length: 30` and `end of response with 30 bytes missing`. After, `500` with `Content-Length: 0` and the connection stays open.

## Assistance Disclosure

Claude Code (Claude Opus) helped write this patch and its test. I reviewed every line, and I ran the test before and after the change and the manual check above myself.
commit_message:
templates: Delete file headers on any template error (#8149)
* templates: Delete file headers on any template error

A template that fails to parse or execute (not only {{httpError}}) left
the Content-Length, Etag and related headers set by file_server on the
error response, so clients received a 500 that declared the file's size
but had no body.

* templates: Also delete Content-Encoding and Content-Range on errors

Precompressed and ranged file responses could leave these headers on the
replacement error response.
task_text:
# templates: a template error keeps file_server's Content-Length, so the 500 has a broken body ### Issue Details When a template fails for any reason other than `{{httpError}}` (a parse error, an unknown function, a failed `include`, ...), the error response keeps the headers `file_server` set for the template file: `Content-Length`, `Etag`, `Last-Modified`, `Accept-Ranges`. The response declares the file's size but has no body, so the client gets a broken response. This is the same symptom as #5902. #5905 fixed it for `{{httpError}}` only, by deleting those headers inside `funcHTTPError`. Every other template error still takes the old path. Version: v2.11.7 (release binary) and master at 8507b63. Caddyfile: ``` :9080 { root * . templates file_server } ``` `bad.html` (30 bytes): ```

hello {{ nosuchfunc }}

``` ``` $ curl -v http://localhost:9080/bad.html > GET /bad.html HTTP/1.1 > Host: localhost:9080 > User-Agent: curl/8.18.0 > Accept: */* > < HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error < Accept-Ranges: bytes < Content-Length: 30 < Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 < Etag: "dlwqvly2ic5a-u" < Last-Modified: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:00:21 GMT < Server: Caddy < Vary: Accept-Encoding < * end of response with 30 bytes missing curl: (18) end of response with 30 bytes missing ``` With a `handle_errors { respond "err {err.status_code}" }` block the error page is also wrong: the response still says `Content-Length: 30`, the body is the 7 bytes `err 500`, and curl reports `end of response with 23 bytes missing`. Expected: the same clean 500 that `{{httpError 500}}` gives today (no `Content-Length` from the file, no `Etag`/`Last-Modified`). The cause is in `modules/caddyhttp/templates/templates.go`: `executeTemplate` returns the error without touching the headers the next handler wrote. Deleting the same headers there, in the error branch, fixes every template error at once. I have a small patch with a test and can open a PR if this sounds right. ### Assistance Disclosure AI used ### If AI was used, describe the extent to which it was used. Claude Code (Claude Opus) helped write the reproduction, the patch and its test. I reviewed every line and re-ran the steps above myself.
gold_patch:
diff --git a/modules/caddyhttp/templates/templates.go b/modules/caddyhttp/templates/templates.go
index de847f66..48ae0dc7 100644
--- a/modules/caddyhttp/templates/templates.go
+++ b/modules/caddyhttp/templates/templates.go
@@ -497,6 +497,16 @@ func (t *Templates) executeTemplate(rr caddyhttp.ResponseRecorder, r *http.Reque
 
 	err := ctx.executeTemplateInBuffer(r.URL.Path, rr.Buffer())
 	if err != nil {
+		// Delete some headers that may have been set by the underlying
+		// handler (such as file_server) which may break the error response.
+		rr.Header().Del("Content-Length")
+		rr.Header().Del("Content-Type")
+		rr.Header().Del("Etag")
+		rr.Header().Del("Last-Modified")
+		rr.Header().Del("Accept-Ranges")
+		rr.Header().Del("Content-Encoding")
+		rr.Header().Del("Content-Range")
+
 		// templates may return a custom HTTP error to be propagated to the client,
 		// otherwise for any other error we assume the template is broken
 		if handlerErr, ok := errors.AsType[caddyhttp.HandlerError](err); ok {
diff --git a/modules/caddyhttp/templates/tplcontext.go b/modules/caddyhttp/templates/tplcontext.go
index e7222183..8f4c3b63 100644
--- a/modules/caddyhttp/templates/tplcontext.go
+++ b/modules/caddyhttp/templates/tplcontext.go
@@ -473,6 +473,8 @@ func (c TemplateContext) funcHTTPError(statusCode int) (bool, error) {
 	c.RespHeader.Header.Del("Etag")
 	c.RespHeader.Header.Del("Last-Modified")
 	c.RespHeader.Header.Del("Accept-Ranges")
+	c.RespHeader.Header.Del("Content-Encoding")
+	c.RespHeader.Header.Del("Content-Range")
 
 	return false, caddyhttp.Error(statusCode, nil)
 }

new file mode 100644
index 00000000..7cea7f12
--- /dev/null
+++ b/modules/caddyhttp/templates/templates_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,65 @@

+package templates
+
+import (
+	"errors"
+	"net/http"
+	"net/http/httptest"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2/modules/caddyhttp"
+)
+
+func TestServeHTTPErrorDeletesFileHeaders(t *testing.T) {
+	for i, tc := range []struct {
+		body       string
+		wantStatus int
+	}{
+		{body: `{{httpError 404}}`, wantStatus: http.StatusNotFound},
+		{body: `{{nosuchfunc}}`, wantStatus: http.StatusInternalServerError},
+		{body: `{{include "missing.html"}}`, wantStatus: http.StatusInternalServerError},
+	} {
+		tmpl := &Templates{MIMETypes: defaultMIMETypes}
+		next := caddyhttp.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) error {
+			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")
+			w.Header().Set("Content-Length", "123")
+			w.Header().Set("Etag", `"abc"`)
+			w.Header().Set("Last-Modified", "Mon, 02 Jan 2006 15:04:05 GMT")
+			w.Header().Set("Accept-Ranges", "bytes")
+			w.Header().Set("Content-Encoding", "gzip")
+			w.Header().Set("Content-Range", "bytes 0-122/456")
+			_, err := w.Write([]byte(tc.body))
+			return err
+		})
+
+		w := httptest.NewRecorder()
+		r := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/index.html", nil)
+
+		err := tmpl.ServeHTTP(w, r, next)
+		handlerErr, ok := errors.AsType[caddyhttp.HandlerError](err)
+		if !ok {
+			t.Fatalf("Test %d: expected a handler error, got %v", i, err)
+		}
+		if handlerErr.StatusCode != tc.wantStatus {
+			t.Errorf("Test %d: expected status %d, got %d", i, tc.wantStatus, handlerErr.StatusCode)
+		}
+		for _, name := range []string{"Content-Length", "Content-Type", "Etag", "Last-Modified", "Accept-Ranges", "Content-Encoding", "Content-Range"} {
+			if got := w.Header().Get(name); got != "" {
+				t.Errorf("Test %d: expected %s to be deleted, got %q", i, name, got)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+}
